subject: Urban Planning
title: Digital Twins for Infrastructure
description: A quick, practical guide to Digital Twins for Infrastructure.

hook.text: Singapore has a complete digital twin of its entire city — every pipe, cable, and building modeled in real time.

buildup.text: A digital twin mirrors physical infrastructure with sensors and data. Engineers can simulate failures before they happen.

discovery.text: When a pipe shows stress in the digital twin, crews fix it before it breaks. Predictive maintenance replaces emergency repair.

twist.text: Most cities don't know where their pipes are. Maps are on paper, outdated, or lost. Digital twins need data cities lack.

climax.text: Building digital twins of aging cities means mapping every buried asset — a project costing decades and billions.

punchline.text: They don't know where the pipes are. Let alone how to model them.

quiz.question: What is the biggest challenge in creating digital twins for existing cities?
options: The computing power required exceeds current technology
Most cities lack accurate records of where infrastructure is buried
Privacy laws prevent sensors from being installed on infrastructure
